title: Public Health Line: Bat in a Child's Bedroom, 230th Street

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Public Health Front Desk (transfer to Director)

callee.name: Naomi Eshleman, RN
callee.label: County Public Health Director (transferred from front desk 555-0132)

transcript.speaker: Front Desk
transcript.text: Calder County Public Health, this is the front desk. Okay, I'm going to put you through to the Director. One moment, please.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Hi, yes, thank you. I'm calling from out on 230th Street, north of Larkin. We woke up this morning and there was a bat flying around my daughter's bedroom. She's seven.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My husband got it in a coffee can with a lid and it's sitting in the garage right now. It's still alive, I think. She says it didn't touch her, but she was asleep, so how would she know?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: And with all the bird flu talk on Facebook this morning, people saying it's spreading and there's trucks all over out here, is this related? Can bats carry that? Do we bring the bat in somewhere? Does she need shots? I have to call the school by ten and tell them if she's coming in.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Okay. So we just leave the can in the garage and don't open it? And somebody calls me back today about the shots? Okay. My number is 555-0163. Thank you, I'm sorry, I know you're probably swamped.

voiceStyles.Front Desk: Woman in her 50s, calm, practiced receptionist, quiet office behind her
voiceStyles.Caller: Woman in her 30s, anxious and talking fast, kitchen sounds and a child's voice faint in the background, steadies once she gets clear instructions

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. It is a routine rabies exposure: a bat in the room of a child who was asleep. Look for the CPH to tell the caller quickly that it has nothing to do with avian influenza, have her keep the bat contained for testing, and hand the case to the duty nurse for a post-exposure prophylaxis assessment. The CPH should then go back to follow-up for the 37 exposed workers and not spend EOC time on this call.
